title: Decompose prefetch threadpool into evented loop and simplify KV bookkeeping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Our continuous prefetching component currently uses a dedicated threadpool for prefetch workers and a separate ad-hoc KV bookkeeping layer that tracks active leases and pending handoffs. This architecture causes tail-latency spikes under high multiplexing (p95 token latency increases ~18% in staging under synthetic skewed workloads) and has high contention on the bookkeeping lock.

Goals: 1) Replace the prefetch worker threadpool with a single evented loop (reactor) that uses cooperative scheduling to reduce context-switch overhead and improve fairness across model lanes. 2) Simplify KV bookkeeping into a lean, append-only reconciliation stream with a compacted index (reduces lock hold time and eliminates a wide lock used during lease reconciliation). 3) Clean up scheduler handoff so that handoffs are event notifications rather than synchronous blocking calls. 4) Preserve SLOs and provide a safe rollback path.

Non-goals: This ticket intentionally avoids touching admission control heuristics, batching window algorithms, or kernel selection logic — those are covered in separate initiatives.

Design summary: - Event loop: single reactor per shard that multiplexes I/O, prefetch tasks, and timer events. Prefetch tasks become lightweight state machines that yield when waiting on I/O or KV state. - Bookkeeping: move from a mutable map guarded by a global mutex to an append-only log of operations (claim, release, prime, evict). A compacting background task produces a small in-memory index for hot keys. Reads use lock-free snapshots when possible; writes append then notify the reconciler. - Handoff API: scheduler will push a non-blocking notification to the target shard; the target enqueues a lightweight callback to accept or defer based on current resource token counts. - Observability: add new metrics (prefetch_coop_yields, kvc_reconcile_ops, handoff_deferred_count), tracing spans around reconciliation windows, and a dashboard panel to compare p50/p95 before/after.

Rollback plan: Ship behind a feature flag per-cluster. Start with canary shards (5% traffic) for two hours, run synthetic skew tests and our existing perf harness. If errors > 0.1% or p95 regression > 10%, flip feature flag off and revert the config-only change.

Success criteria / Acceptance: - No increase in error rate attributable to new code during canary. - p95 end-to-end generation latency reduced or unchanged; p50 improved by at least 8% in lab runs. - KV bookkeeping CPU usage (wall) reduced by >=12% under the measured skewed workload. - New metrics and dashboard panels populated and alerts configured.

Implementation plan (high level): 1) Extract current prefetch worker logic into a state-machine library (small refactor PR). 2) Implement reactor and integrate state-machine for prefetch on a single shard locally. 3) Build append-only bookkeeping layer and compatibility shim for reads/writes. 4) Replace scheduler handoff to use non-blocking notifications, implement deferral queue. 5) Add metrics, tracing, and dashboard updates. 6) Canary rollout behind feature flag and run perf suite.

Artifacts: - Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime-modernization/prefetch-event-loop - Prototype benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-perf/tree/eng/539007-prefetch-reactor - Initial PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls?q=is%3Apr+539007
comments: 2026-02-16 - Marcus C: Spiked a local prototype; evented loop reduced thread count by 60% and p50 for prefetch tasks by ~22%. Still seeing a few reconciliation bursts at high write rates. Logging attached to the prototype branch.

2026-02-20 - Aisha P (Design review): Approved architecture direction. Requested explicit contract for snapshot consistency between append-only log and compacted index. Added requirement to support a quick full-index rebuild during shard restart.

2026-02-24 - Marcus C (Engineering): Implemented append-only ops with lightweight compactor. Initial unit tests added for idempotent replay. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4871 - awaiting code review.

2026-02-26 - Gabriela S (SRE): Concern about GC pressure in the compactor; suggested using a ring-buffer-backed journal to avoid short-lived allocations. Marcus to prototype ring buffer approach next week.

2026-02-28 - Marcus C: Benchmarks on staging harness (skewed 80/20 access): p95 generation latency reduced by 12% on canary shard under 1k QPS. KV bookkeeping CPU decreased by 15%. Pushed a metrics patch to staging. Note: one flaky test around lease reordering found; added to follow-up.

2026-03-01 - Code review feedback: Request to add more end-to-end tests covering handoff deferral path and to document invariants for the compactor (order, idempotence). Also requested observability for deferral queue length.

2026-03-02 - Marcus C: Addressed most review comments, added tests for deferral path, and instrumented deferral queue. Planning canary rollout next week behind feature flag runtime.prefetch_reactor=true. Will coordinate with SRE for rollout playbook.
